start-at-the-outcome.title: Start at the outcome
start-at-the-outcome.script: Here is one possible response to the party example. Start from the intended outcome, rather than copying today's roles into the workflow. The roles tell you who is available; the outcome helps show what the plan needs.

contract-on-every-milestone.title: Contract on every milestone
contract-on-every-milestone.script: Then make the important handoffs checkable, without prescribing every step inside the task. Agree what needs to arrive and how the result can be checked; the person or agent doing the work can choose how.

cut-seams.title: Cut seams
cut-seams.script: Finally, look for handoffs that add no reviewable value. In this example, combining related work is one possible redesign—not a rule that fewer steps are always better.

not-more-meetings.title: Not more meetings
not-more-meetings.script: Remember the question from the first Slide? More meetings were one possible answer. In this example, clearer goals and handoffs address the gaps; another workflow may need something else.
